conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released and the FY EBIT guide (EUR 300-350m) sits above a company-compiled consensus of EUR 306m, so a low-end narrowing is largely priced. Two inferences offset each other: consensus gross-margin expansion (+110bp) looks conservative against Q2's +200bp, while peer EMEA prints in Q3 (Puma -11.5%, Moncler -8%) cast doubt on the implied sales improvement. The structural fact is that Frasers holds about 49-50% plus 21.87% via sold puts, and bought on 23 Oct at about EUR 38.26, roughly 1-2% under spot. That cushions the downside and damps the move (20-day realised vol 7.6% annualised). Hence abs 4.0 (below the 7% new-numbers base because of the controlling holder), p_up 53, scaled +0.24, against a findings sum of +0.2. The two measurements agree.

already_public.what: FY2026 outlook reaffirmed with Q2: currency-adjusted sales down mid- to high-single digits, EBIT EUR 300-350m, EMEA down high-single digits to low teens, Americas/APAC down low to mid single digits
Company-compiled (Vara) consensus: Q3 sales EUR 919m, GM 62.3%, EBIT EUR 81m (range 75-93, n=9); FY26 EBIT EUR 306m (288-314)

Frasers crossed 50% of voting rights (50.08%, plus 21.87% through sold put options), then 49.41% after an instrument exercise on 27 Oct. Frasers does not rule out buying more shares in the next 12 months.
No Prognoseanpassung ad-hoc filed since the Q2 release. The only ad-hocs were the buyback termination (1 Sep) and the chairman change (14 Sep).

new_in_release.expect: Q3 sales/GM/EBIT against EUR 919m / 62.3% / EUR 81m. GM is likely at or above consensus and sales at risk below it. Net: roughly in line.
Likely the FY EBIT guide reiterated, or narrowed toward the low end of EUR 300-350m. Consensus 306 already prices the low end. A cut below 300 is the tail risk and is not the base case.
Probably still strong: inventories were down 15% y/y at Q2 and FCF before leases was EUR 137m in H1. Mildly supportive, direction otherwise unknown.
Possible capital-allocation or dividend commentary under Frasers control (buyback terminated 1 Sep; reports of dividend-policy tension). Direction unknown.
October/Q4 start commentary. Unknown, though the peer tone in Europe is weak.

findings.finding: Frasers controls about 50% directly, carries a further 21.87% exposure through sold puts, bought 198,666 shares for about EUR 7.6m (about EUR 38.26 each) on 23 Oct, and says it does not rule out further purchases. A disclosed buyer about 1-2% below spot cushions a disappointing print and damps the reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the 10 Jun bid the stock has traded EUR 37.5-39.1. The Q2 print on 4 Aug moved -0.03% (it was inside the offer period). Frasers buying days in late October moved it +0.8% to +1.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The level is priced: spot of 38.7 already sits on Frasers' buying. What may not be priced is the asymmetry on a miss. If the market priced it fully, implied downside would be near zero, but a hunter has no option chain to confirm that. 20-day realised vol of 7.6% annualised is consistent with a pinned stock.
findings.independence: Frasers' purchase price and the 50.08% stake were reported independently at https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/frasers-takes-control-of-hugo-boss-as-stake-crosses-50/2026102591026

findings.finding: Consensus Q3 gross margin of 62.3% implies +110bp y/y, versus +200bp in Q2 and +160bp in H1, with inventories down 15% y/y (fewer markdowns). At consensus sales and opex -4% (as in Q2), a Q2-like GM gives EBIT of about EUR 86-91m against an EUR 81m bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024: EBIT 95 vs about 90 consensus with guide held, and the stock rose (baseline history +5.59 around 2024-11-07, estimated date). The Q2 2026 beat was absorbed by the offer pin.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is visible, but its GM step-down from Q2's +200bp is an analyst choice, not a company statement. If the market expected a GM beat, the consensus range top (EBIT 93) would anchor it, and it does not. This is an inference from the company's own H1 numbers, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 GM +200bp and inventories -15% come from the company release https://group.hugoboss.com/en/investors/publications/financial-releases/publication/hugo-boss-drives-claim-5-touchdown-execution-in-q2-and-reaffirms-2026-outlook (same company, different document)

findings.finding: Peer Q3 prints show European apparel demand still weak (Puma EMEA -11.5% currency-adjusted with Middle East spillover, Moncler EMEA -8%, adidas Europe -4%). That makes consensus Q3 sales of EUR 919m (-7% reported, after -10% in Q2) a stretch for a company that is about 60% EMEA.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 sales of -10% were 'in line' and did not move the stock (offer pin). In Q3 2025, flat sales with the guide at the low end gave -2.51% (estimated date).
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer proxies, and Boss already guides EMEA down high-single digits to low teens, so most of this is inside the guide. It is sized near zero. It would be fully priced if consensus Q3 sales sat nearer EUR 895m, a Q2-like decline.

findings.finding: FY consensus EBIT of EUR 306m sits at the bottom of the EUR 300-350m guide and implies H2 EBIT of EUR 212m (-15% y/y) after H1 -34% (EUR 94m vs about 142m). The release is likely to narrow to the low end, which is priced, but a Q3 sales miss could tip the guide below 300.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: guide confirmed but 'at the lower end', stock -2.51% (estimated date in baseline history).
findings.why_not_priced: The low end is priced: consensus is 306, not the 325 midpoint. The residual is the tail of a cut below 300, which no estimate source below 288 reflects. It is sized small because it lands inside the guide.
findings.independence: Guide and 2025 base EBIT of EUR 391m: https://group.hugoboss.com/en/investors/publications/financial-releases/publication/hugo-boss-drives-claim-5-touchdown-execution-in-q2-and-reaffirms-2026-outlook

findings.finding: Q2 carried mid-single-digit EUR millions of one-off takeover-defence costs in administration expenses. Q3 spans the additional acceptance period (to 13 Aug) and the supervisory-board changes, so reported Q3 EBIT likely carries further one-off advisory costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history: this is the first takeover period.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts may not have put Q3 one-offs into 'EBIT reported' consensus. The item is a one-off with no path to the guide, so it is a fraction of its EBIT size.

lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move' / 'Understatement is the hunters' systematic error': abs_move_pct raised from 3.5 to 4.0. It stays below the 7% new-numbers base because the controlling holder and 7.6% realised vol are a structural damper. Expected move goes from +0.21 to +0.24.
'In a live bid, results are noise': checked. The offer period ended 13 Aug, so it does not apply directly, but it supports keeping abs_move below base. No finding changed.
'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number': checked, and there is no Prognoseanpassung ad-hoc. The quarter is not pre-released. No change.
